content: A first checkpoint of a newly created canonical package still commits its complete canonical file set.

A re-checkpoint after modifying only a subset of an existing package commits exactly that changed canonical subset and succeeds only when the checkpoint commit tree contains the complete validated canonical package file set with matching hashes.
An exact replay returns already-checkpointed without an additional commit, and inspect validates the latest partial re-checkpoint from the complete commit tree.
Existing unrelated staged-state, symlink, race, wrong-root, and failure-cleanup behavior remains unchanged.
A focused regression test fails before implementation and passes afterward.
Checkpoint distinguishes changed commit paths from complete canonical package tree and hash verification.
The focused artifact handoff test suite passes.
Only the two approved implementation and test files change during scoped execution.
AI review evidence and Human review material are recorded.
